findings.rationale: The document-generation path verifies every signed approval against a TrustStore, but `document check` exposes no trust-key option and `load_approvals_for_check` merely parses V2 records and copies their key IDs. A forged or untrusted signed record can therefore be incorporated into the expected rendering and reported as `document_conformant`, falsely presenting stakeholder approval as valid.

`unassigned_init_state_vars` marks an entire state root assigned when any component is written in any branch. `concrete_initial_states` then enumerates only wholly absent roots, default-initializing untouched map keys, struct fields, or conditionally unwritten values. Since `check_refinement` relies on this set for implementation and abstraction initial states, legal nondeterministic initial states can be omitted and an invalid refinement can pass.

Migration plans and validates content read before `atomic_write_migrations`, but the write phase never verifies that each target still contains those bytes. A concurrent editor or migration can change a file after planning; the later rename silently overwrites that newer content. Backups are created only at commit time and are deleted on success, so they do not prevent or recover this lost update.

Although coverage tracking can merge assignments to separate struct fields, `init_write_key` collapses every field target to the root variable. After `s.a` is assigned, a subsequent disjoint `s.b` assignment is therefore reported as assigning `s` twice. Valid deterministic field-by-field initialization is rejected by the explicit engine and forces `auto` verification to fall back unnecessarily.
